review_notes: Read the whole target file (201 lines) plus the closely analogous non-dependent file Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean and Mathlib/Data/Finset/Finsupp.lean, and checked the supporting API in Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Defs.lean (mk_apply, mk_of_mem, support_subset_iff, mem_support_iff, notMem_support_iff, mk_injective), Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/Order.lean (support_inf_union_support_sup), Mathlib/Data/DFinsupp/BigOperators.lean (prod, prod_of_support_subset), Mathlib/Data/Finset/Pi.lean (mem_pi), Mathlib/Data/Finset/Lattice/Basic.lean (notMem_union, subset_union_left/right, notMem_mono), Mathlib/Data/Multiset/AddSub.lean and Defs.lean, and Mathlib/Order/Interval/Finset/*. No execution was possible, so all proposed replacements are untested suggestions phrased as concrete tactic blocks, not claims that they compile. Several proofs (card_Ico/Ioc/Ioo/Iio, card_uIcc, mem_pi, rangeIcc, mem_singleton_apply_iff, rangeIcc_apply, card_Icc, card_dfinsupp) already reduce to a single named lemma or a two-line rewrite, and were deliberately not flagged as golf candidates because no simplification preserving readability was identified.

findings.excerpt:
(fun f g x => by
      refine (mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset support_rangeIcc_subset).trans ?_
      simp_rw [mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff, forall_and]
      rfl)
findings.problem: The final step closes the goal with `rfl` after `simp_rw` has already unfolded `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff` and pushed `forall_and` into the goal. `rfl` gives the reader no hint about what the remaining goal is (the conjunction `(∀ i, f i ≤ x i) ∧ ∀ i, x i ≤ g i`, i.e. the order on `Π₀`), and the proof relies on `simp_rw` having rewritten the goal into exactly the shape that is definitionally equal to the order relation on DFinsupp. The non-dependent analogue in this repository makes the last step explicit as `forall_and`.
findings.proposed_change:
Mirror the `Finsupp` proof: keep the `mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset` refinement, rewrite only with `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff`, and end the proof with the named fact:

    (fun f g x => by
      refine (mem_dfinsupp_iff_of_support_subset support_rangeIcc_subset).trans ?_
      simp_rw [mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff]
      exact forall_and)
findings.benefit: The reader sees that the pointwise order on `Π₀` is precisely the conjunction of the pointwise inequalities supplied by `Finset.Icc`, which is the mathematical content of the `LocallyFiniteOrder` instance. Using `exact forall_and` instead of a bare `rfl` after a compound `simp_rw` also keeps the proof robust if the `simp` set for `mem_rangeIcc_apply_iff` changes.

findings.excerpt:
· rintro ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
    rw [Function.Embedding.coeFn_mk]
    refine ⟨support_mk_subset, fun i hi => ?_⟩
    convert mem_pi.1 hf i hi
    exact mk_of_mem hi
findings.problem: The only use of `mk_of_mem` in this direction is inside a `convert ... ; exact mk_of_mem hi` pair: `convert` generates the side goal that the embedded value equals the `mk`-value on the membership proof, and the next line discharges exactly that with `mk_of_mem`. This is an intermediate stepping stone that a reader must reconstruct: two steps (a `convert` plus an `exact`) where one `simpa` using the named fact expresses the same reasoning directly.
findings.proposed_change:
Collapse the two steps into one rewriting step that names the key lemma:

  · rintro ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩
    rw [Function.Embedding.coeFn_mk]
    refine ⟨support_mk_subset, fun i hi => ?_⟩
    simpa only [DFinsupp.mk_of_mem hi] using mem_pi.1 hf i hi
findings.benefit: The forward direction of the membership characterisation is exactly `mem_pi` transported through `DFinsupp.mk_of_mem`; making that the whole step, with `mk_of_mem` visible in the `simpa` set, shows the reader the single mathematical move instead of a `convert` whose only purpose is to trigger the subsequent `exact`. It also removes the fragile `convert`, which depends on the definitional shape of the embedded function.

findings.excerpt:
intro x hx
  by_contra h
  refine notMem_support_iff.2 ?_ hx
  rw [rangeIcc_apply, notMem_support_iff.1 (notMem_mono subset_union_left h),
    notMem_support_iff.1 (notMem_mono subset_union_right h)]
  exact Icc_self _
findings.problem: The proof works with `h : x ∉ f.support ∪ g.support` but never splits it: instead it derives the two components implicitly through `notMem_mono subset_union_left h` and `notMem_mono subset_union_right h`. The actual case analysis (the point is in neither support, hence both values are zero, hence the `Icc` collapses to a singleton containing zero) is hidden inside two `notMem_mono` applications, and the two `notMem_support_iff.1` rewrites silently perform the `x ∈ f.support ↔ f x ≠ 0` transport.
findings.proposed_change:
Split the union membership explicitly and use `notMem_support_iff` directly on each component, e.g.:

  intro x hx
  by_contra h
  rw [Finset.notMem_union] at h
  refine notMem_support_iff.2 ?_ hx
  rw [rangeIcc_apply, notMem_support_iff.1 h.1, notMem_support_iff.1 h.2]
  exact Icc_self _
findings.benefit: The reader sees the whole argument in one line: outside the union means both `f x = 0` and `g x = 0`, so the pointwise interval is `Icc 0 0`, which contains `0`. The `notMem_mono`/`subset_union_left` plumbing becomes unnecessary, and the only facts used are the two named characterisations of support membership.
